assumptions_made.assumption: Approval thresholds are converted to US dollars at 18.0 MXN and 5.5 BRL to the dollar. The configuration format expresses every approval threshold in a single USD field, while Logística Globex sets thresholds in three currencies.
assumptions_made.source:
politica_gastos_2026.txt, section 5.2 (line 68) — document owner Joaquín Esparza (Gerencia de Contabilidad, Monterrey), authorising a reasonable documented exchange rate for system configuration: "utilizar un tipo de cambio razonable y
    documentarlo; la precisión cambiaria NO es crítica para los límites de tarjeta"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Approval thresholds shift with the rate. The 2,000 MXN Mexican auto-approve threshold becomes $111.11, and the 20,000 MXN manager threshold becomes $1,111.11. These rates were not taken from a rate provider — no live rate source was available — so both rates must be confirmed before go-live. Accounting uses Banco de México and Banco Central do Brasil month-end closing rates for consolidation, which are the authoritative figures.

assumptions_made.assumption: Spending limits themselves are NOT converted. Every limit is recorded in the currency of the entity that holds it — pesos in Mexico, reais in Brazil, dollars in Miami — exactly as requested.
assumptions_made.source: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt — Alejandra Vidal (Directora de Finanzas (CFO), Logística Globex), [02:27], requiring that limits and reports stay in each entity's local currency: "Los límites, los reportes, todo en moneda local. En Brasil igual: reales. En Miami, dólares."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: None expected. Ramp supports a currency per limit, so this requirement is met directly and no exchange rate touches a card limit. Only the approval thresholds needed conversion, and only because the configuration format has a single USD field for approval thresholds.

assumptions_made.assumption: No email address is recorded for anyone. This packet contains no address and no email domain, so every address is written as N/A rather than constructed.
assumptions_made.source: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt — Alejandra Vidal (Directora de Finanzas (CFO), Logística Globex), [04:37], naming the two account administrators without giving any email address, as is the case for everyone in this packet: "Yo y Joaquín, mi gerente de contabilidad."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: No user can be invited until Logística Globex supplies real addresses. Thiago Moreira is the sharpest case: the call states a company email already exists for that person, but the address itself is not in the packet.

assumptions_made.assumption: The Brazilian entity is recorded with status 'requested' rather than 'existing', and the three Brazilian drivers are recorded with a note that the accounts must not be activated until the entity exists.
assumptions_made.source: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt — Alejandra Vidal (Directora de Finanzas (CFO), Logística Globex), [00:42], stating that the Brazilian entity is still in formation: "São Paulo está en proceso."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If the entity is created earlier than expected the Brazilian setup can be activated sooner. If it slips past October, the three drivers start work without cards, which the policy memo explicitly requires to be ready on the drivers' first day.

assumptions_made.assumption: Ramp can hold the Brazilian users in a draft state, created but not invited, and activated later. This answers the question the call asked directly.
assumptions_made.source: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt — Alejandra Vidal (Directora de Finanzas (CFO), Logística Globex), [05:09], asking whether staff can be set up without being activated, and asking not to be given an invented answer: "Si el sistema permite dejarlos listos sin activar, mejor. Si no, díganme qué se puede y qué no — no me inventen."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: None to the mechanism, which is native. This configuration format has no field for the draft state, so it is recorded in each user's notes rather than as a setting.

assumptions_made.assumption: Departments are recorded once and shared across all three entities. Ramp departments are company-wide.
assumptions_made.source: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt, line 19 — Rubén Ortega (Director de Operaciones, Logística Globex), [01:18], describing the Mexican organisational structure that the other entities will mirror: "Tres áreas grandes. Operaciones — choferes, supervisores de patio, coordinadores de ruta."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: A person in Brazilian Operations and a person in Mexican Operations sit in the same department. If Logística Globex needs to report or target spend by country and department together, that combination is not available through departments alone.

assumptions_made.assumption: Locations are recorded for Monterrey, Miami and São Paulo, but this configuration format cannot bind a location to a legal entity — locations carry only a name and a country.
assumptions_made.source:
politica_gastos_2026.txt, line 10 — document owner Joaquín Esparza (Gerencia de Contabilidad, Monterrey), listing the three legal entities the policy covers: "Esta política aplica a todo el personal de Logística Globex, S.A. de C.V. (México),
Globex Logistics USA LLC (Miami) y Globex Logística do Brasil Ltda. (São Paulo,
en constitución)."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: The three entities appear in this configuration but nothing in it attaches a person to one. In Ramp the attachment is made through the location, so the deployment owner must make that link during setup. This is a limitation of the configuration format, not of Ramp.

assumptions_made.assumption: Elena Ruiz is given the Business Admin role, which is company-wide. The request was for an administrator scoped to Miami.
assumptions_made.source: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt — Alejandra Vidal (Directora de Finanzas (CFO), Logística Globex), [04:37], describing a per-country local administrator model: "en cada país va a haber un administrador local cuando arranquen — en Miami ya sabemos que es Elena Ruiz, la gerente de oficina"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Elena Ruiz can see and administer Mexican and Brazilian spend as well as Miami's, which is broader than intended. Entity-restricted roles exist in Ramp but are a paid tier and are configured in the application — see the unsupported requests section. Confirm the plan tier, or accept the wider access knowingly.

assumptions_made.assumption: The figure 2,000 MXN carries two unrelated meanings in this packet and is recorded as two separate things: the per-transaction ceiling on minor parts for yard supervisors, and the Mexican auto-approval threshold.
assumptions_made.source: politica_gastos_2026.txt, section 2.2 (line 21) — document owner Joaquín Esparza (Gerencia de Contabilidad, Monterrey), setting a per-transaction ceiling on minor parts, a different rule from the approval threshold that shares the same figure: "Incluye casetas y refacciones menores (< $2,000 MXN por transacción)."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Conflating the two would either cap all supervisor spend at the approval threshold or let minor parts bypass approval. The two are separate rules that happen to share a number.

assumptions_made.assumption: Driver fuel cards are restricted to the fuel category rather than to a list of named fuel stations, because no list of authorised stations appears in the packet.
assumptions_made.source: politica_gastos_2026.txt, section 2.1 (line 18) — document owner Joaquín Esparza (Gerencia de Contabilidad, Monterrey), requiring that driver cards work only at authorised fuel stations: "Solo estaciones de combustible autorizadas. Sin excepciones."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: A driver can buy fuel at any station Ramp classifies as fuel, not only at the authorised ones. The memo says this restriction has no exceptions, so the gap is material. Ramp can restrict to named merchants, but the list of authorised stations has to be supplied first.

assumptions_made.assumption: Reimbursements remain enabled. The policy memo eliminates reimbursements from Q4 2026, and both the memo's own inline note and the call override that for road expenses.
assumptions_made.source: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt — Alejandra Vidal (Directora de Finanzas (CFO), Logística Globex), [05:45], instructing that operational reality overrides the memo on reimbursements: "El memo es aspiracional en esa parte. [ríe] Hazle caso a Rubén."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If reimbursements are switched off, drivers cannot recover cash spent at road hotels that take no cards, which is the situation the operations director described. The memo's stated goal is preserved as a direction of travel, not as a configuration.

assumptions_made.assumption: The Administración card covers office expenses only, not software subscriptions, despite the call describing it as covering subscriptions.
assumptions_made.source: politica_gastos_2026.txt, section 2.4 (line 24) — document owner Joaquín Esparza (Gerencia de Contabilidad, Monterrey), defining the Administración allowance as office expenses, with software handled centrally in the following section: "Gastos de oficina (Administración): $5,000 MXN mensuales por persona."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If Administración staff are expected to buy subscriptions directly, those purchases will decline. This reading follows the centralised-software requirement, which is stated in both sources and more forcefully — see the conflicts section.

assumptions_made.assumption: Route coordinators are deliberately excluded from this configuration, and Miami fuel is deliberately excluded.
assumptions_made.source: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt, line 27 — Rubén Ortega (Director de Operaciones, Logística Globex), [02:15], excluding route coordinators from card issuance: "Los coordinadores de ruta no necesitan tarjeta; ellos no gastan."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: None expected. Both exclusions are stated explicitly, and Miami fleet spend is to be rejected and escalated to Monterrey rather than configured.

assumptions_made.assumption: This audit log and the configuration are written in English. The executive summary requested in Spanish is a separate document and is not produced by this pipeline.
assumptions_made.source: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt — Alejandra Vidal (Directora de Finanzas (CFO), Logística Globex), [05:57], requiring the executive summary in Spanish because the board reads Spanish: "el resumen ejecutivo que me mandes, en español por favor. Mi consejo lo lee en español."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: The board receives nothing readable if the Spanish summary is not written separately. This is a delivery obligation the two JSON files cannot satisfy, and it must not be lost.

missing_information_flags.question: What are the email addresses for Alejandra Vidal, Rubén Ortega, Joaquín Esparza, Elena Ruiz and Thiago Moreira? Every address is recorded as N/A because the packet contains none. The call states Thiago Moreira already holds a company address, but the address itself was not provided.

What are the names and email addresses of the roughly sixty Mexican employees who need spend capability, and of the three Brazilian drivers starting in October? None are named, and the Brazilian cards are required to work on the drivers' first day.

What is the list of authorised fuel stations? The memo says driver cards must work only at authorised stations with no exceptions, and no list is given, so the cards are currently restricted to the fuel category rather than to named merchants.

Are the exchange rates used for approval thresholds acceptable — 18.0 MXN and 5.5 BRL to the dollar? These were not taken from a rate provider. The thresholds are the only figures in this configuration affected by a rate; every card limit stays in local currency.
Who will administer São Paulo? The administrative team there has not been hired, so Brazil currently has no local administrator.

Should the Administración card cover software subscriptions or office expenses only? The call describes it as covering subscriptions, while the memo assigns software to a central card. Encoded as office expenses only — see the conflicts section.
Which Comercial staff travel to Brazil and the United States, and do those trips draw on the Mexican peso limit or on a local one?
When will the Brazilian commercial team be hired? The memo sets a travel allowance for that team conditional on it existing.
Who else works in the Miami office besides Elena Ruiz, and how many people need cards there?
Should receipts or memos be required above any threshold? Neither is mentioned anywhere in this packet.

conflicts.description: Whether cash reimbursements continue. The policy memo eliminates reimbursements from the fourth quarter of 2026 and requires all spend to go on a corporate card. The operations director recorded a dissenting note inside that same memo, and repeated it on the call: many Mexican road hotels accept only cash, so drivers cannot recover expenses without reimbursements.
conflicts.source_a: politica_gastos_2026.txt, section 2.6 (line 28) — document owner Joaquín Esparza (Gerencia de Contabilidad, Monterrey), eliminating cash reimbursements from Q4 2026: "Los reembolsos en efectivo quedan ELIMINADOS a partir del Q4 2026."
conflicts.source_b: politica_gastos_2026.txt, section 2.6 (line 31) — document owner Joaquín Esparza (Gerencia de Contabilidad, Monterrey), dissenting inline within the same memo, in a note dated three days after the memo version: "Mantener reembolsos para hoteles/alimentos en ruta."
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Reimbursements remain enabled. The CFO settled this on the call by naming the memo aspirational on this point and instructing that the operations director be followed. Two independent signals agree — the inline note inside the memo itself, and the CFO's spoken instruction — so this is resolved rather than open. Recorded because the memo, as the standing written policy, still says the opposite.

conflicts.description: Whether the Administración card covers software subscriptions. The call describes the 5,000 peso Administración card as covering subscriptions and office items. The memo defines the same allowance as office expenses, and separately requires all software to be bought on one central card held by Sistemas, with every new vendor approved by Finance beforehand.
conflicts.source_a: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt, line 37 — Rubén Ortega (Director de Operaciones, Logística Globex), [03:16], describing the Administración card as covering subscriptions and office items: "tarjeta virtual con límite bajo, cinco mil pesos al mes, para suscripciones y cosas de oficina"
conflicts.source_b: politica_gastos_2026.txt, section 2.5 (line 25) — document owner Joaquín Esparza (Gerencia de Contabilidad, Monterrey), assigning all software to a single central card held by Sistemas: "Software (centralizado, Sistemas): $25,000 MXN mensuales, tarjeta única virtual."
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded as office expenses only, with software excluded from the Administración card. Centralised software purchasing is stated in both sources and stated more forcefully, including a requirement that every new vendor be approved before the first purchase. Allowing subscriptions on a second card would defeat that control. Raised as a question because the two statements are minutes apart on the same call.

conflicts.description: The memo describes itself as not internally harmonised, and its three sections were written by three different authors in three languages. No amount actually conflicts between the sections, because each section governs a different entity, but the document's own warning is recorded so the absence of conflict is understood as checked rather than assumed.
conflicts.source_a: politica_gastos_2026.txt, line 5 — document owner Joaquín Esparza (Gerencia de Contabilidad, Monterrey), warning that the memo's sections are not fully harmonised: "Nota interna: documento de trabajo. Las secciones no están totalmente armonizadas entre sí."
conflicts.source_b:
politica_gastos_2026.txt, section 5.3 (line 71) — document owner Joaquín Esparza (Gerencia de Contabilidad, Monterrey), setting the language precedence rule for resolving discrepancies: "Cualquier discrepancia entre versiones de idioma de este documento se resuelve
    a favor de la versión en español, excepto la Sección 4, cuyo original es el inglés."
conflicts.provisional_resolution: No language discrepancy was found that required the precedence rule. Sections 2, 3 and 4 cover Mexico, Brazil and Miami respectively and do not overlap, so there is no competing statement of the same figure in two languages. The rule remains available if one emerges: Spanish wins except in Section 4, whose original is English.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: The São Paulo entity, Globex Logística do Brasil Ltda., which is still in formation and expected at the end of September.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Legal entities are created in the Ramp application rather than through the API. This configuration records the Brazilian entity as requested rather than existing, which is the honest answer to the question asked on the call: the design can be completed now, but the entity itself has to be created by hand once the lawyers finish.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — /entities is GET-only; the separate POST /accounting/entities creates an accounting-side object, not a Ramp legal entity. docs.ramp.com accounting guide, checked 2026-08-30 — 'Entities are created in the Ramp UI, and objects are scoped to an entity_id when fetching via the API.'
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Legal entities are created in the Ramp application, not through the API. The entity is recorded here as requested and the people belonging to it are prepared without being invited, so the deployment owner creates the entity first and the accounts are activated once it exists.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Three approval chains, one per country, with equivalent rather than identical local thresholds: 2,000 and 20,000 pesos in Mexico, 400 and 4,000 reais in Brazil, 100 and 1,000 dollars in Miami.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp has no endpoint for creating approval policies. All three chains are recorded here as desired state and must be built in the Ramp application. A second constraint is specific to this customer: this configuration format expresses thresholds in a single US dollar field, so the local figures have been converted and the original amounts preserved in each policy's source line. Ramp itself does not impose that limitation.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — no approval-policy write endpoint; only /blank-canvas-approvals/* (acts on existing instances) and GET /spend-programs/{id}/workflow-nodes (read-only); zero approval OAuth scopes. support.ramp.com 'Set up your spend approval policies', checked 2026-08-30 — tiered approval chains ARE configurable in Ramp's in-app approvals workflow builder, so this is a UI-only capability rather than a missing one.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Tiered approval chains are a standard Ramp feature, but are built in the approvals workflow builder inside the Ramp application rather than through the API. The tier structure requested is recorded here as desired state, and the deployment owner recreates it in Ramp before go-live. Routing by amount and by user role is available on every plan; more elaborate conditions require Ramp Plus, so confirm the plan tier first.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Approval by the Finance Directorate before the first purchase from any new software vendor, whatever the amount.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: The rule depends on whether a vendor is new, not on the amount, and Ramp approval rules trigger on amount. A rule that catches every new vendor also catches every existing one, so the policy recorded here routes all software spend to the CFO, which is broader than requested.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — no approval write surface; additionally 'new vendor' is not threshold-shaped and approval_policies[].tiers[] is keyed only on threshold_usd_cents.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp cannot route an approval on the basis that a supplier is new; approval rules are driven by amount and by user role. The closest available control is a dedicated spend program for first-time suppliers with a low approval threshold, set up by the deployment owner in the Ramp application, accepting that it will also stop ordinary purchases above that amount. This requirement is therefore recorded as a process control rather than an automated one.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: A local administrator in each country, seeing and administering only that country's spend.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp scopes spend visibility by reporting line rather than by entity. Entity-restricted roles do exist for multi-entity customers, but sit in a paid tier and are configured in the Ramp application rather than through the API. Elena Ruiz is therefore recorded with company-wide administrative access, which is wider than the Miami-only intent.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: support.ramp.com 'User roles overview', checked 2026-08-30 — transaction visibility follows the reporting chain, not department labels, and manager permissions are scoped to the manager's own team; that chain is settable via direct_manager_id on POST /users/deferred. Finer scoping (Custom Roles, entity restriction) exists in-app on Ramp Plus but is not API-creatable — Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) shows GET /roles is read-only.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp scopes spend visibility to a manager's own reporting line, so setting each person's manager correctly delivers most of this requirement directly. Anything beyond that — visibility that does not follow reporting lines — requires a Custom Role, which is configured in the Ramp application and is available on Ramp Plus. Confirm the plan tier before relying on it.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Departments that belong to a specific legal entity, so that Mexican Operations and Brazilian Operations are distinguishable.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp departments are company-wide and carry no entity association. The three entities are recorded, and each person's location is recorded, but nothing in this configuration format binds a location to an entity — that link is made in Ramp during setup.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — the department create body is name-only with no entity_id, so departments are company-wide; only locations carry an entity association.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Departments in Ramp are account-wide and cannot be attached to a legal entity; only locations carry an entity association. The requested split is preserved either by modelling it through locations or by naming each department with its entity prefix, and the deployment owner should confirm which of the two reads better in reporting.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: One limit per role covering all drivers, all yard supervisors, the commercial team and the administrative team.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp limits belong to one person, so each of these becomes one limit per member. Roughly sixty people in Mexico need spend capability, of whom about forty are in Operations, and none are named in this packet.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — POST /funds requires a single user_id, so a group limit becomes one fund per member; is_shareable with /funds/{id}/members is the nearest shared-pool primitive and has different semantics (one shared pot, not N).
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp attaches a spend limit to one person at a time, so a limit described for a team becomes either a separate limit of that size for each member or a single shared pot the whole team draws down. Those are materially different outcomes and the wording of a request rarely settles which is meant, so the deployment owner should confirm the intent for each team-level limit before setup.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Driver cards that work only at authorised fuel stations, with no exceptions.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp can restrict a card to named merchants, so this is achievable, but no list of authorised stations appears in the packet. Until that list is supplied the cards are restricted to the fuel category instead, which is broader: any station Ramp classifies as fuel will work.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — blocked_vendors / blocked_vendor_ids take merchant UUIDs from GET /merchants (not Bill Pay vendor objects); no global blocklist resource exists, so the block must be repeated on every spend program and standalone limit.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: A merchant block is real and enforced, but Ramp holds no account-wide blocklist: the block is set on each spend program and each individual limit, and must be re-applied to anything created later. The deployment owner should add that step to the routine for issuing new cards and programs. One trade name can also map to more than one merchant record in Ramp, so each name is resolved separately.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Physical cards for the whole commercial team and virtual cards for administration and for the central software card.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp creates virtual cards as part of issuing a spend limit rather than on request. Physical cards must be requested individually and require a shipping address for each holder, and this packet contains no addresses.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — POST /cards/physical exists (requires shipping_address and user_id) but virtual cards are GET-only and are issued via funds rather than created directly.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Both card types are available: a virtual card is issued alongside a spend limit, while a physical card is ordered explicitly and needs a shipping address for each recipient. Shipping addresses are not present in the material provided, so the deployment owner supplies one per physical cardholder before those cards can be ordered.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Onboarding roughly sixty Mexican staff, plus Miami and Brazilian staff as those offices open.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp creates users one at a time rather than from a file. At this volume that is a loop rather than an obstacle, but the three openings are staggered — Mexico in four weeks, Miami in about six, Brazil when the entity exists — so this happens three times rather than once.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — no bulk user endpoint; POST /users/deferred is per-user and async (poll /users/deferred/status/{task_id}), with idempotency_key required in the body.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp has no bulk user import: people are created one at a time and each creation is processed in the background. At the volumes described this is not a practical constraint, since the roster is loaded in a single automated pass rather than typed in, and each request carries a duplicate-protection key so a re-run of a weekly wave cannot create the same person twice.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Adjusting the central software programme as subscriptions consolidate onto it.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp spend programmes cannot be edited through the API once created, so the software programme should be reviewed carefully before it is created.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — /spend-programs has GET and POST only and /spend-programs/{id} is GET-only; there is no PATCH or DELETE, so programs are immutable via the API.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: A spend program cannot be edited through the API once created; later changes are made in the Ramp application instead. That makes the review of program definitions before go-live the cheapest point to change anything, and the deployment owner should treat it as the moment to settle names, limits and restrictions.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Distinct permission levels for a CFO, an accounting manager, an operations director, a Miami office manager and a Brazilian operations manager.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp offers a fixed set of roles with no seniority or scoping dimension, so each job title is matched to the closest available role. Every non-obvious match is listed in the assumptions above.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) plus support.ramp.com 'User roles overview', checked 2026-08-30 — Ramp exposes six assignable roles with fixed, documented permission sets and no seniority or scoping dimension, so mapping customer job titles onto Ramp roles is a per-person judgement call.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp offers a fixed set of six assignable roles with defined permissions and no seniority or scoping dimension, so each job title is matched to the closest role by judgement rather than by rule. Every non-obvious match is recorded with the job title, the role chosen, and what that role can see and do, for the deployment owner to confirm before invitations go out.
